mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 1.5% compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days as the monetary policy stance remains accommodative.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 1.5% (vs baseline positive rate of 65.5%), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points from the prior month signals labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp (vs baseline negative rate of 34.1%), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential investment (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) from the prior month indicate broad demand weakness, triggering equity sell-offs as revenue growth expectations decline, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline from prior month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when HOUST and RSAFS both decline (vs baseline negative rate of 34.1%), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100) indicates manufacturing slowdowns and supply chain disruptions, increasing input costs and reducing corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 100 (vs baseline negative rate of 34.1%), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly non-farm payrolls decline below 100,000 new jobs (PAYEMS < 100) signals labor market weakness, reducing consumer confidence and spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS < 100 (vs baseline negative rate of 34.1%), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Residential investment above 1,200 thousand units (HOUST > 1200) indicates strong housing market conditions, boosting consumer confidence and corporate capital expenditure, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST > 1200 (vs baseline positive rate of 65.5%), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous federal funds rate decline (FEDFUNDS < 1.5%) and consumer price index increase (CPIAUCSL > 245) indicate stagflationary pressures, triggering equity sell-offs as real rates rise, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines and CPIAUCSL > 245 (vs baseline negative rate of 34.1%), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 245) signals the Federal Reserve will tighten monetary policy, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 245 (vs baseline negative rate of 34.1%), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
